bullets.title: US-Iran Strike Pause Triggers 6-7% Oil Drop, Sparks Equity Relief Rally
bullets.body: US paused Iran strikes for a second consecutive night after Omani diplomats arrived in Tehran for Strait of Hormuz talks; Iran suspended retaliatory attacks conditionally. WTI crude fell ~6.5% to $83.54/bbl and Brent dropped ~7.5%, while S&P 500 futures rallied ~0.9% to 7515 and NDX futures gained ~1.6%. Oil's sustained disruption—middle-east crude exports down from 13.6 mb/d to 8.4 mb/d—remains a key macro tail risk, with each additional month of conflict adding ~$7-8/bbl to Brent and geopolitical tension over the Strait unresolved.

bullets.title: FOMC Week: Market Prices ~32-38% Hike Odds; Base Case Is Hold, But Oil Shock Changes Calculus
bullets.body: Fed holds rates at 3.50-3.75% with July hike odds at 32-38% and September hike odds at ~72-82%, up sharply from early July as energy inflation re-escalates. UBS, Goldman, and 22V all expect no hike this week; Fed Chair Warsh and Governor Waller cited persistent supply shocks as rationale for potential tightening. A 1-2 hike scenario with modest financial-conditions tightening is the base case, which 22V views as supportive of cyclicals (Banks, Retail, Transports, Homebuilders); 4+ hikes would be unambiguously bad for risk assets.

bullets.title: Q2 Earnings Season Blazing: 86-88% EPS Beat Rate, 37.9% Blended Growth—But Stocks Fade on Print
bullets.body: With ~27-35% of S&P 500 market cap reported, blended Q2 EPS growth is +37.9% YoY (ex-Google's $98B Anthropic gain, still +25.9%); 86% beat EPS estimates vs. 78% 5-year average, and 82% beat revenue vs. 70% average. Despite strong prints, stocks are averaging a -0.3% move on beat days with a -4% reaction to misses—JPM's tactical buy signal triggered at -1.5z positioning (US 19th percentile). EPS guidance momentum is at highest since 2011 with 1.3x more above-consensus than below-consensus guides, and S&P 1500 margin sentiment at 91.6th percentile.

bullets.title: Mega-Cap Tech Earnings This Week Are the Critical Catalyst: META, MSFT Wed; AAPL, AMZN Thu
bullets.body: 34% of S&P 500 market cap reports this week including four Mag-7 names: META ($60.2B rev / $7.18 EPS) and MSFT ($87.6B / $4.24) Wednesday; AAPL ($108.9B / $1.89) and AMZN ($196.8B / $1.82) Thursday. The Mag-7 basket fell ~5-6% last week as AI ROI concerns and GOOGL's capex shock drove de-grossing—JPM notes HFs net-sold Mag-7 at -1.5z over 5 days. AAPL is the outlier, outperforming NDX by ~22 percentage points in July (best month vs. Nasdaq in 20 years) on memory/FCF discipline and Apple Intelligence momentum.

bullets.title: Nvidia Backstops $250B OpenAI Ohio Data Center; SK Group $500B+ AI Partnership Locks Memory Supply
bullets.body: Nvidia is in advanced talks to guarantee ~$250B financing for OpenAI's 10-gigawatt Ohio campus (total project >$500B including chip purchases), while simultaneously announcing a $500B+ initiative with South Korea's SK Group covering AI factory deployment and HBM4 next-gen memory co-development with SK Hynix. Samsung signed a $200B+ MOU with Broadcom spanning memory, foundry (2nm), and advanced packaging through 2030. Cumulatively, Korea announced ~$950B in AI/semiconductor partnerships in one week, reshaping the AI supply chain landscape.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler Capex Shock: GOOGL Raises 2026 Guidance to $195-205B; AI Capex Framework Now $1.34T by 2027
bullets.body: Google's 2Q capex doubled YoY to $44.9B and raised 2026 guidance by $15B; GOOGL also disclosed $514B GCP backlog (+385% YoY) and $707B future committed spend through 2030. UBS updated aggregate AI capex to $1.34T in 2027E and $1.48T in 2028E. GOOGL reported negative FCF of ~-$5.9B in 2Q; debt expanded from ~$16B to ~$100B over the past year. The capex shock triggered a 7% GOOGL selloff and cascaded to broader AI infrastructure names (hyperscaler CDS at multi-year highs, ORCL 5Y CDS at record wides).

bullets.title: Semis Entering Multiple-Compression De-Rating Phase; Investor Sentiment Shifts to 'Prove the Economics'
bullets.body: Semiconductor multiples compressed sharply: memory -24%, CPUs -21%, optical -15%, semicap -18% from recent highs. Jefferies notes median tech EPS-day move is -300bps—largest downside skew in 50 quarters—while HFs have net-sold semis for 4 consecutive weeks. Morgan Stanley argues AI infrastructure dip is a buying opportunity (Jevons Paradox intact; compute demand durable), while JPM flags global semis long/short at 98th percentile, signaling crowding risk persists. The 10-year yield at 4.65-4.70% is the amber-warning threshold for real equity impact.

bullets.title: AI Cost Deflation Accelerating: Chinese LLMs Dominate OpenRouter Usage at 58%; Token Prices Down 29% from May Peak
bullets.body: Chinese AI models (DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, MiniMax) now account for ~58% of AI token usage by US firms on OpenRouter, surpassing US models for the first time. Open-weight model pricing surged +36% MoM and +74% YoY as they gain share (10% to 20% of total spend). Closed-weight models still represent 80% of total spend despite 29% of volume. The Silicon Data LLM Token Expenditure Index declined to 1.47-1.58 from 2.04 in May, reflecting enterprise shift to cost-efficient models and multi-model routing strategies.

bullets.title: Data Center Power Demand Revised Sharply Higher: BloombergNEF Base Case 118GW by 2030 vs. Prior 77GW
bullets.body: US data center power demand base case revised to 118GW by 2030 (up from 77GW), with an aggressive AI-chip scenario at 160GW. Individual campus sizes now exceed 10GW vs. traditional 1GW. Grid interconnect lead times are 48-84 months and heavy electrical equipment 36-60 months—creating a massive gap vs. AI hardware lead times of 3-12 months. Of 434GW proposed Texas capacity, only 11GW (2.5%) is under construction; execution risk is rising with local/state pushback and inexperienced developers.

bullets.title: Memory Prices Spiking: DRAM DDR5 Up 890% YoY; Deceleration Expected in Q3 to +16% QoQ
bullets.body: DRAM spot prices (DDR5 16Gb) reached $50.83 in July, up 890% YoY and 17% MoM. B200 GPU rental prices accelerated +7.3% MoM to $5.72/GPU-hr (2.13x premium to H100), while H100s dipped -1.1% MoM. Contract price growth for DRAM and NAND is expected to decelerate sharply to +16% and +13% QoQ in Q3 from +56% and +58% in Q2. Memory inventory at suppliers stands at 2.6-2.7 weeks vs. normal 5 weeks; hyperscaler NAND at 3 weeks vs. normal 7 weeks—undersupply thesis intact near-term.

bullets.title: CXMT IPO Surges 465-472% on Shanghai Debut; Raises $85B in Capacity Risk for Micron Long-Term
bullets.body: China's CXMT debuted with a 465-472% first-day gain on Shanghai, making it China's largest onshore-listed company at ~$488B valuation. Near-term the captive HBM supply serves Huawei (not MU's market); MU operates in a different dynamic. Longer term, CXMT's $85B IPO proceeds fund capacity expansion, creating structural DRAM oversupply risks. Chinese HFs reportedly sold Korean semiconductor positions to fund CXMT IPO participation, contributing to Korean equity weakness Friday.

bullets.title: Apple Lobbying White House to Use CXMT/YMTC Memory Chips Outside US; Micron Opposing
bullets.body: Apple is actively lobbying the White House to approve Chinese-made memory chips (CXMT, YMTC) in devices sold outside the US, while Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra is pushing back against the proposal. AI demand has shifted memory bargaining power to suppliers—Apple historically dictated LPDDR prices but now faces 600%+ cost increases. MacBook prices rose $300 despite only ~$100 in underlying memory cost increases, per critics. Qualcomm separately plans double-digit chip price increases from September amid smartphone and memory shortages.

bullets.title: Market Positioning Flashes Tactical Buy Signal; Quality Rotation Underway as Early Cycle Phase Ends
bullets.body: JPM's Tactical Positioning Monitor triggered a buy signal at -1.5z with aggregate US positioning at the 19th percentile. Morgan Stanley and Jefferies both flag a rotation from AI infrastructure spenders (hyperscalers, semis) toward AI adopters and quality names. S&P 500 support is viewed at 7000; August is seasonally flat and September is historically the worst month. 2026 YTD: value and small/mid-caps are outperforming; international/EM outperforming; Mag-7 down.

bullets.title: Open-Source AI Debate Intensifies: Nvidia, Microsoft, Meta, Google, Palantir Back Open Weights; Anthropic Outlier
bullets.body: Jensen Huang, Satya Nadella, Mark Zuckerberg, Sundar Pichai, and Palantir signed an open letter supporting unrestricted open-weight AI models. Anthropic is positioned as the lone significant holdout, drawing criticism from David Sacks and others for lobbying against open-source. Washington is divided between protecting frontier labs (OpenAI, Anthropic) vs. open-source approaches; Polymarket prices 37% odds of US restricting a major Chinese AI model in 2026.

bullets.title: GLW Faces H2 Headwinds: LCD Panel Prices Down 2.1% MoM in July, Expected -2.7% in August
bullets.body: LCD TV panel prices declined 2.1% MoM in July and are expected to fall 2.7% in August vs. seasonal +1.4%—a 16-consecutive-month YoY decline. TV makers are unable to pass higher supply-chain costs (memory BOM inflation) to consumers, widening losses. Chinese TV makers cut Q3 panel demand forecasts; panel makers are considering utilization cuts. GLW's optical enterprise segment remains strong (+28% YoY) but display pricing correction is expected to begin in Q2 results, creating an asymmetric earnings setup.

bullets.title: TSMC 2nm Ramping at 20K Wafers/Month; INTC EMIB-T Could Emerge as Meaningful Second-Source by 2027-28
bullets.body: TSMC's Fab 20 in Hsinchu achieved 20,000 wafers-per-month in 2nm production, the highest among five Taiwan 2nm fabs. Advanced packaging TAM is projected to grow 59% CAGR to $122B by 2030. UBS forecasts TSMC retains 65-70% advanced packaging share in base case with 50% CAGR; Intel's EMIB-T could capture ~13% market share by 2030 with H2 2027-28 mass production target. Nvidia's GB300 'Made in USA' chips have begun rolling off TSMC Arizona production lines.

bullets.title: ECB Signals Another Rate Hike; BoJ Hike Expected December; Fed on Hold; Structurally Higher Neutral Rates
bullets.body: ECB policymaker Kazimir called for at least one more hike; Morgan Stanley expects ECB to hike in September and BoJ in December 2026 (to 1.25%, then 1.50% by mid-2027). The Fed is expected on hold in 2026. AI-driven productivity gains are pushing US real neutral rate estimates sharply higher, which could keep policy tighter for longer. Japan's 40-year JGB yield eased to 4.0%, 20-year to 3.65%; Singapore tightened in a surprise MAS move.

bullets.title: Global IG Bond Funds See $7.1B Record Weekly Outflow; US Margin Debt at $1.5T All-Time High
bullets.body: US investment-grade bond funds saw $7.1B in weekly outflows, the largest since COVID. US margin debt climbed to a record $1.5T in June (+$86.5B MoM, +49% YoY), with leverage relative to GDP at an all-time high. S&P 500 short interest rose to ~3.7% of free float, the highest since 2010. Cash on the sidelines has fallen to a record low. Global bond yields hit their highest levels since the 2008 financial crisis.

bullets.title: Waymo Explores Exit from Uber Partnership; Robotaxi Tension Deepens
bullets.body: Waymo is reportedly exploring options to exit its partnership with Uber in Atlanta and Austin as early as January 2028, ahead of the current contract's May 2028 exclusivity end. Waymo (valued at $126B) plans to offer rides on its own app in those markets, directly competing with Uber's ~200M+ customer base. UBER shares hit new 52-week lows on the report; JPM Internet coverage is down 7% on the week vs. SPX -1%.

bullets.title: GOOGL Raised to Buy at Phillip Capital; Chamath Bullish on $500B Backlog and Compounding ROIC
bullets.body: Phillip Capital upgraded GOOGL to Buy with a $425 PT (33% upside), noting confidence in long-term outlook despite the capex shock. Chamath characterizes Google as a '32% average ROIC compounder since IPO that can win the entire AI stack.' GCP backlog jumped >$50B to $514B; Cloud growth accelerated to 82% YoY on AI demand. Azure 2H26 guidance is for modest 39-40% growth (consensus 41%), with investor target of ~43% by Q2/Dec 2026.
